text: Paul prayed for the Ephesians, already filled with the Spirit, to receive "the spirit of wisdom and revelation." The Holy Spirit in you wants to be asked.
explanation:
The Ephesian believers were among the most spiritual Paul wrote to. They had been baptised in the Holy Spirit. Yet Paul kept praying that God would give them "the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of Him, the eyes of your understanding being enlightened." Isaiah lists seven ways the one Spirit rests on the Messiah, beginning with wisdom and understanding.

The Spirit isn't just a guest who eats dinner and retreats to His room. He wants to sit at your table and counsel you. You can ask Him for wisdom again and again, for your work, your marriage, your children. You have not because you ask not.

text: Revelation doesn't give you something new. It shows you what you already have.
explanation:
A poor elderly woman was once visited by her pastor. He noticed a frame on her wall, and when he picked it up, a paper fell out. It was the will of the wealthy man she'd once worked for, leaving her his entire estate. She'd been living in poverty because she couldn't read.

In Christ "are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge," and "you are complete in Him." Many believers live like that woman, owning everything and knowing nothing about it. That's why Paul prayed "that you may know." Ask God to open the eyes of your heart.

text: Bezalel was a brick-making slave in Egypt. God "filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom," and he built the ark of the covenant.
explanation:
Bezalel had spent his life trampling straw in Pharaoh's brick kilns. He had never worked gold or carved precious stones. Yet God said, "I have filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship." Then He added, "In the hearts of all who are wise-hearted I have put wisdom."

What you lack, God can fill. And notice who receives more: the wise-hearted, those who keep coming to Him hungry. "To him who has, more will be given." Seek Him, and He'll give you skill for whatever He's called you to build.

text: Even Pharaoh, a pagan king, looked at Joseph's wisdom and said, "Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom is the Spirit of God?"
explanation:
Pharaoh had the dream; only Joseph knew what it meant. Joseph not only interpreted it, he added practical counsel nobody had asked for: appoint a discerning and wise man, and store up a fifth of the harvest in the years of plenty.

Pharaoh used Joseph's own words: "There is no one as discerning and wise as you." A slave was promoted to rule Egypt in a single day. The world is hungry for real wisdom, not just clever thinking. When God's wisdom flows through you, even unbelievers can see the Spirit of God in you.

text: "It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us." Sometimes God's wisdom comes as you talk it through with godly counsellors.
explanation:
The early church faced a heated question: did Gentile believers need to be circumcised? The apostles and elders gathered, argued, listened and prayed, until they could write, "It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us." God doesn't always hand you a finished answer. Often His will grows inside you over time, and gets clearer as you share it with others.

"In the multitude of counsellors there is safety" (counsellors, not a committee). "He who walks with wise men will be wise." For big decisions, don't be a lone ranger. Wisdom is contagious.

text: Abraham kept asking, from fifty righteous down to ten, and God kept agreeing. God didn't stop giving; Abraham stopped asking.
explanation:
When Abraham interceded for Sodom, every time he asked, God said yes. The conversation ended when Abraham stopped asking, not when God stopped answering. When King Joash struck the ground with arrows only three times, the prophet was grieved: he should have kept going.

Prayer isn't a work to earn God's favour; it puts Him in His rightful place as the Giver. Daniel prayed for what God had already promised through Jeremiah, and an angel was dispatched the moment he began. Keep asking. Your limited asking is the only limit on His supply.

text: Joshua was "full of the spirit of wisdom." The very next thing God told him was to meditate on His Word day and night.
explanation:
Moses laid his hands on Joshua, and he was filled with the spirit of wisdom. Then, as the book of Joshua opens, God tells him: "This Book of the Law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate in it day and night… then you will have good success."

Having the Spirit of wisdom doesn't make the Word unnecessary. It makes you treasure it more. Scripture is the treasure house of God's wisdom, and "health to all their flesh" for those who find it. The more wisdom God gives you, the hungrier you'll be to open His Book.
